hypothesis: The neuron responds selectively to prominent, straight vertical lines or bars that act as dividers, frames, or structural supports within the image. These features consistently manifest as elongated, continuous vertical strips—such as white metal window mullions, silver railing bars, truck locking rods, slot machine dividers, or furniture legs—that segment the visual space into rectangular regions. The activating elements are typically neutral or metallic in color, specifically white, silver, grey, or black, and maintain a sharp structural contrast against backgrounds that vary widely in color and texture. The neuron remains invariant to the semantic category of the object (e.g., architectural vs. mechanical) and lighting conditions, as long as the strong vertical linearity is preserved. The activating feature typically occupies 50–100% of the image height, often spanning the entire frame and frequently appearing as multiple parallel lines distributed across the width.
